newsitem.title: FINLAND: Estonia says near border deal with Russia.
newsitem.headline: Estonia says near border deal with Russia.

text.p: Estonian Foreign Minister Siim Kallas met Russian counterpart Yevgeny Primakov on Tuesday to end a long-running border row and said he was optimistic an agreement could be reached by the end of the year.
The two sides have been arguing over their border since Estonia quit the former Soviet Union in 1991.
They agree where the border should lie but Estonia wanted Russia to recognise a 1920 peace treaty as part of the package.

"We are optimistic for agreement this year," Kallas told a news conference in the Finnish capital, en route from his meeting with Primakov in the northwestern Russian town of Petrazavodsk to Strasbourg.

The 1920 Tartu treaty has huge symbolic and legal value for Estonians as in it Russia agreed to respect Estonia's independence. Twenty years after it was signed, Estonia was annexed by the Soviet Union.
Russia said the treaty was no longer relevant and refused to recognise it.
The Estonian foreign ministry said in a statement that a draft treaty has been prepared and there would be no changes.
However, neither the ministry nor Kallas mentioned how the problem of the Tartu peace treaty would be overcome.
Kallas insisted any border deal would not go against the treaty, which is a politically sensitive subject in Estonia.
"The border treaty will not be against this (the Tartu) treaty and will not damage this treaty and it will not be against the Estonian constitution," he said.
Estonia is anxious to wrap up a border deal as a dispute with Russia may be an obstacle in its aim to enter the European Union (EU) and NATO.
